facts.statement: Ningyuansaurus is classified as a pennaraptoran dinosaur genus.
facts.quote: Ningyuansaurus is a pennaraptoran dinosaur genus.

facts.statement: The only known species, Ningyuansaurus wangi, is known from a single fossil specimen found in the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation in western Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: It contains the single species Ningyuansaurus wangi, known from a fossil specimen from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation (Aptian stage, 124.6 Ma ago) of Jianchang, western Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen dates to approximately 124.6 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
The species name 'wangi' honors Wang Qiuwu, the private owner who donated the fossil for study.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Wang Qiuwu, the private owner of the specimen who donated it for scientific study.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen is currently housed in the Confuciusornis Museum in Xingcheng.
facts.quote: The specimen is now in the Confuciusornis Museum in Xingcheng.

facts.statement: The dinosaur had relatively large eyes.
The skull was generally triangular and longer than other basal oviraptorosaurs, featuring a straight lower jaw unlike most of its relatives.
facts.quote: The skull was generally triangular in shape but longer than other basal oviraptorosaurs like Caudipteryx, with a straight lower jaw unlike most other oviraptorosaurs.

facts.statement: The arms were short, with the upper arm bones (humeri) being longer than the lower arm bones (ulnae).
facts.quote: The arms were short, with longer upper arms (humeri) than lower arms (ulna).

facts.statement: The legs were long, with the femur being longer than the pelvic bones.
facts.quote: The legs were long, and the upper leg (femur) was longer than the pelvic bones.

facts.statement: The tail was relatively long and preserved feather impressions near the tip.
facts.quote: The tail was relatively long and feather impressions were found near the tip.

facts.statement: While originally thought to be the most basal oviraptorosaur, later research reclassified it as a member of Halszkaraptorinae.
facts.quote: It was originally thought to be the basalmost species of oviraptorosaur, based on its long skull and a greater number of teeth in comparison to any other known oviraptorosaur. However, later research showed that it is a member of Halszkaraptorinae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses by Cau and Madzia (2021) placed Ningyuansaurus in varied positions within the dinosaur family tree.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Cau and Madzia (2021) placed Ningyuansaurus within varied positions.

facts.statement: The time range for Ningyuansaurus is estimated from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
